title: Eratosthenes measures the circumference of the Earth
summary: Eratosthenes of Cyrene, working as librarian at Alexandria, compared the noon Sun on the summer solstice at Syene (modern Aswan), where it shone down a well, with the shadow cast at Alexandria. Taking the cities as 5,000 stadia apart and the angle as 7.2 degrees, he reached 250,000 stadia for the whole circumference; other accounts give 252,000.

uncertainty.note: The opened pages date the measurement to about 240 BCE (Encyclopedia.com) and about 220 BCE (Linda Hall Library); another page opened for context gives about 245 BCE (ABC News). The range runs from 245 to 220 BCE.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the date: three opened pages give about 240 BCE, about 220 BCE, and (on a page used only as context) about 245 BCE, so the year is a decade-level approximation. Pin is Alexandria; Syene (Aswan) is the second point. The 250,000 and 252,000 stadia figures both appear in opened pages; no conversion to kilometres is claimed.
